Evidence: `node/src/fork_resolution.rs:146`, `node/src/payment_transition.rs:46`,
`:212`, `node/src/trst_storage.rs:192`, `node/src/ledger_updater.rs:394`.
The fork path restores BRN, holdings and graph, validates bases/rebuilds indexes,
then persists full economics after applying the replacement. Row replacement
collects an old-key BTreeSet and visits the complete new state. This adds global
decode/validation/encoding and O(N log N) key bookkeeping for N replaced rows;
BRN persistence visits every wallet. It is not the ordinary live delta path.
BRN restoration has 131,072-entry / 64 MiB limits: these bound/reject work and
do not demonstrate lifetime scalability. Exceeding a cap can prevent recovery.

Fix: scoped restoration and replay overlays based on authenticated undo and
dependency closures. Do not substitute live caches that describe the losing
branch. Reuse existing fork/replay fixtures; first measure one local replacement
with increasing unrelated state, then dependent replacement batches. Full
snapshot import is naturally global; paying it per replacement is the concern.

Follow-up source review, 2026-10-20: `payment_transition::apply_authenticated`
and `fork_resolution::apply_candidate` both restore from the writer and then
call full `persist_economics`. The existing `StagedEngines` already supports
lazy candidates and transactional BRN/TRST/graph deltas, including legacy
storage fallbacks and row before-image checks. A candidate baseline can come
from the freshly restored **rewound writer**, without consulting live
losing-branch engines. Reusing that machinery could remove full-state
republication while preserving the global restore/validation step. That is
only a partial CX12 fix; it must not be described as scoped restoration.
Before implementation, cover both payment-only and verification/governance
fork callers, return/publish ownership, legacy and row formats, non-tail undo,
failed replacement and restarted state. Existing payment-transition shared-
staging/abort tests and fork/rollback fixtures are the starting point; no new
driver is needed.

Fork publication implementation, 2026-10-20: payment-only replacement and
verification/governance fork execution now borrow their freshly restored
writer state through `StagedEngines`. Economic, verification and governance
transitions use existing staged APIs; token counters inspect the candidate;
publication uses the existing BRN/TRST/graph delta writers. Returned engines
take changed candidates or the restored originals after persistence succeeds.
No live losing-branch cache is consulted. Legacy aggregate fallbacks remain.
This removes unconditional full republication, not the global restore,
validation/index rebuild, affected-portfolio work or lifecycle snapshots.
The existing merge replacement regression now runs both legacy and row storage,
including aborted evaluation, replacement, restart and 32 unrelated BRN wallets.
Node compilation passed in 1m57s and its receipt verified. Affected runtime

Implementation update, 2026-10-20: account-pending RPC now selects through a
transactional amount-descending index, with source hash as the equal-amount tie
breaker. Threshold and offset cursor semantics are preserved. LMDB traverses
O(offset + page + 1) index entries after seeking, and fetches/decodes only page
payloads (each primary lookup also has database tree-search cost). It no longer
loads and sorts the entire account backlog. First-page work is bounded by page
size plus payload sizes; arbitrary deep offsets remain linear. The trait's
compatibility fallback still loads/sorts all entries for other backends.

The new `pending_amounts` table fits within the existing 32-table limit. Direct
writes, batched writes, undo and checkpoint replacement maintain it atomically.
Checkpoint verification checks both primary coverage and index cardinality.
The existing pending-index version advances from 1 to 2; opening old state
atomically rebuilds the derived indexes before committing that marker. Older
binaries reject version 2. This startup migration scans all pending entries and
adds durable index storage; no production database was migrated in these tests.

Evidence: `node/src/governance_commit/activation.rs:43`,
`governance/src/engine.rs:1018`, `trst/src/engine.rs:1417`.
TRST expiry-parameter activation scans every token, including expired tokens
that can become active again: O(T), plus changed portfolio copies/persistence.
This follows protocol semantics and is not automatically an algorithmic bug.
Governance activation preview/check also clones the complete governance engine.
Closed proposals, ballots, origins, graph revisions and expired tokens must have
an explicit retained-working-set/archive policy; caps on single messages do not
provide that policy.

Fix: remove unrelated engine cloning, maintain indexes by effective origin time,
and evaluate versioned/lazy expiry normalization with a consistent activation
cut. Any batched implementation must expose an atomic state boundary; accepting
payments against partially migrated rules is unsafe. Define required scale and
maximum pause budgets before choosing migration or archival semantics. Retain
appeal, resurrection, fork and historical-proof dependencies.

and the period before publication. Raw accumulation is checked, indexed errors propagate,
and governance activation/recovery callers propagate failure. No holdings are saturated,
dropped or partially activated. New engine/node fixtures cover valid expired historical
value above u128, earlier-wallet rollback, exact-max success, recovery view failure and
approved activation abort/reopen. Library validation passed371 tests, including raw/retained atomic rejection and
exact-max success. Node propagation validation passed54 selected tests (14.034s summed runtime), including
expiry-view rejection and approved activation abort/reopen. Build plus54 runtime receipts
audit pass/reuse; exact identities are in the ledger. The activation fixture tests the
approved-proposal component, not reachability through a fully admitted adversarial history. Global O(t)/O(t log t) activation work remains budgeted separately.

## Operation-by-operation map

The costs below are local work **plus** the explicitly listed shared findings.
Every accepted block also pays bounded-format authentication, predecessor/account
lookups, ledger/undo writes, and token-counter refresh: bounded warm cache lookup
plus wallet lookup. Matching retained cuts now use timestamp-prefix sums (at most
64 radix branches); **raw/context-mismatched cuts and overflow fallback still scan O(t)**.
Fifty selected node tests and the distinct-deadline counter diagnostic passed; full-payment/release qualification and order-sensitive runtime cost remain outstanding.
Its semantics
count nonrevoked amounts expired at the requested timestamp (including Expired rows
evaluated at earlier times), and checked revoked sums. The original warm storage diagnostic omitted counters; its distinct-deadline extension
measures this API separately, but neither establishes whole-payment scaling.
Optional stake-release acknowledgements add CX02/CX11 even to otherwise simple
operations. These are admission costs, not end-to-end distributed finality costs.

| Operation | Local work and shared costs | Improvement priority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open, empty | Fixed ledger initialization; no need to assume a global economic clone | Preserve cheap empty path |
| Open with pending | Receive delivery below; pending value/provenance size matters | CX03/CX08 |
| Burn → mint | BRN balance O((a+1) log r); persistent BRN wallet path/touched value; origin registration and pending output; affected TRST value/edge work remains | CX02/CX03 qualification; CX11 partial |
| Send | Matching retained cut: origin-scoped debit O(q log t), O(b log b) provenance ordering; candidate due projection and pending write additional. | Receive | O(b+c) provenance validation plus revision queries; retained insertion O((b+c) log(t+b+c)); raw vectors retain detachment/shifts. Checked stable cache can retain new/changed portfolios; counter qualification remains | CX03/CX08/CX10 |
| RejectReceive | Pending validation and return pending creation proportional to stored provenance; no immediate generic receive delivery in this branch | Preserve point lookup; bound/measure provenance |
| Merge, explicit | Retained O(m log t) selection; raw expected O(t+m); retained removal O(m log t) with targeted deindexing, raw O(t) pass; shared parent-edge trees and indexed durable positions; affected portfolio and qualification costs remain | CX03/CX08 partial/CX09 |

| Stake return / acknowledgement | Sorted proof insertion; O(1) release total; outcome-keyed acknowledgement; selection stops at full page; has-more uses nonempty count/outcome lookup and bounded scan; selection worst-case scan remains | CX11 partial |
| Expiry / expired pending return | Warm held schedule/dirty-counter selector skips unchanged holders. Retained token expiry visits due entries; affected counter scans and cold/backward/context rebuild remain. Legacy pending returns use the generation-bound origin-time index: cold O(Q log Q), warm changed-key/due-row work plus due-key ordering. Certified replay still scans Q pending entries at agreed cuts | CX07 warm selector fixed; qualify cold/due bursts and certified replay separately |

Unsupported mixed cuts retain global restore; checked revision inverses now retain the cut. Constitutional diff application itself, verifier sampling, ORV election internals,
network queues, full checkpoint export/import, pruning and every convenience RPC
are not fully bounded by this table. They remain follow-up coverage, not an
implicit clean bill of health. `BlockType` is the operation inventory here;
public library helpers and background protocol transitions are a broader set.

## What already helps and must be preserved

- Ordinary live admission uses staged engines and changed-row persistence, not
  full payment restoration on every block.
- Row-format migrations exist. Legacy aggregate fallback is not evidence that
  every current live node writes aggregate TRST snapshots on each payment.
- Shared snapshots skip unchanged containers and portfolios; delta persistence
  checks stored before-values before publication.
- Merge fan-in is capped at 256; release references at 1024; content at 512 KiB
  and amendment text at 50,000 characters; scoped grant records at 2048 bytes.
  Applicable feature release gates remain relevant.
- Origin/holder reverse indexes avoid scanning unrelated wallets for each
  revocation; graph propagation uses a visited set and topological traversal.
- Balance caches and earliest-expiry checks exist. A current cached transferable
  balance can be O(1); full candidate validation and counters are not.
- Pending destination ranges and sender indexes already exist. Improve pagination
  through these indexes instead of adding a duplicate pending store.
- Governance delegation traversal has a depth bound. Never describe it as an
  unbounded recursion attack without establishing different reachable code.

## Implementation and validation queue

This is the original sequencing checklist. The per-finding updates and current
completion-ledger handoff supersede completed steps: retained counter prefixes,
keyed persistence, cache publication and several graph/pending indexes already exist.
Do not interpret an initial prescription below as evidence that its implementation
is still missing. Remaining work must be selected from the recorded residual costs
and unqualified scopes, with source/receipt review before scheduling.

1. Preserve scoped debit/library/node evidence. CX01 release qualification remains
   open. Remove changed-wallet O(t) token-counter scans before claiming full-payment
   scaling from retained engine/cache microdiagnostics; preserve arbitrary signed
   timestamps, expiry periods, revoked amounts and checked overflow semantics.
2. Qualify lazy governance/verification access and persistent BRN changes (CX02);
   qualify persistent TRST engine/graph maps and their structural deltas (CX03).
3. Split governance/verification persistence into transactional scoped records;
   make proposal reads targeted and version their projections (CX04–CX06/CX13).
4. Make idle expiry proportional to due work; then remove positional token write
   amplification and repeated parent-edge scans (CX07–CX09).
5. Profile affected graph/revision overlap; qualify indexed rate/pause accrual
   and optimize retained releases while preserving exact lifecycle semantics
   (CX10/CX11).
6. Apply the same scoped state model to fork/recovery; qualify global activation
   and retained-history limits on the validation host (CX12/CX15).

For measurements, vary one dimension at a time: unrelated wallets, wallet tokens,
same-origin fragments, proposal/ballot history, electorate/depth, shared graph
descendants, revision history, pending backlog, rate/pause counts. Use geometric
sizes within the existing caps. Record stage time for admission, clone/detach,
economic transition, delta discovery, serialization, writer/commit and publication;
also rows visited/written, bytes allocated and lock hold time. A microbenchmark
of a hash lookup or cheap snapshot clone cannot establish transaction scalability.

Existing bases: `brn/benches/brn_bench.rs`, TRST engine tests (including same-origin
debit and shared snapshots), `economic_candidate/staging/tests.rs`,
`trst/engine/record_delta` tests, graph storage tests, governance ballot/delegation
tests, governance/verification commit tests and expiry commit tests. Extend them
instead of adding a new validation framework or regenerating an expensive ledger.
Their presence was inspected; no historical test pass is claimed as newly verified.

### R2 query execution gap and commitment evidence reconciliation — 2026-10-21

100–100k voters, five samples and1,000 cached accesses per sample. The100k receipt

42.105ns per cached call; neither proves release/full-node query throughput.

Concrete remaining implementation gap: handlers/governance_projection.rs page/info
call Reader::capture and project_snapshot synchronously on the async HTTP task.
Node GovernanceReader performs storage capture and potentially cold restores in
that call; project_snapshot performs due tallies on a miss. The bounded result
cache deliberately computes outside its mutex and does not coalesce simultaneous
misses. Thus removing live-engine locks did not remove synchronous worker occupancy
or bound duplicate cold CPU work across requests. This is a source finding, not a
measured outage or an assertion that ordinary cached calls are slow.

Existing pagination HTTP tests hold engine locks and prove pinned-view behavior;
they do not test executor responsiveness while capture/tally is blocked. Existing
cache tests cover reentrant completion and stale contexts; preserve those semantics.
The next coherent fix must move production reader capture plus projection off async
workers with bounded in-flight work, retaining permits until actual worker exit
(including request cancellation), and preserve exact snapshot/deadline/error rules.
Extend existing RPC tests with controlled blocking rather than manufacturing a
large ledger. Validate overload, cancellation and current-thread responsiveness;
then run the existing pinned HTTP integration against changed dependencies. An
unbounded spawn_blocking per request is not sufficient. No new timing threshold,
protocol economics, or release acceptance loop is needed for this fix.

### R1 admission concurrency and signed-operation coverage reconciliation — 2026-10-21

Decision25.7 explicitly selects parallel processing of different account chains

these. Completion-plan C14 already identifies the concurrency gap; do not downgrade
it to a benchmark-only omission or declare authentication parallelism sufficient.

Historical source map before the prepared-admission integration below:

| Boundary | Implementation at that review | What it establishes / unresolved work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authentication | block_validation.rs bounded blocking workers, retained FIFO handles | Parallel signature/format work; not parallel economics |
| Admission | node.rs validation_queue.next loop and validate_authenticated_candidate | One candidate advances through economic commit before the next; no independent-account preparation overlap |
| Economic preparation | node.rs Accepted arm holds live BRN/TRST, opens LMDB writer, calls economic_candidate::stage, lifecycle effects and persist | Atomicity/isolation retained, but preparation is serialized along with the mandatory single writer |
| State dependency boundary | economic_candidate.rs stage reads predecessor/account/pending, validates signing grant, applies engines and stages durable block rows | Read validation and mutation are coupled to LmdbWriteTransaction; no general optimistic prepared-read-set adapter was found in scoped source search |
| Publication | Engines publish only after batch commit; processor/frontier update follows | A parallel change must retain this order and avoid overwriting another account's committed roots |
| Confirmation | backlog registration and consensus follow admission | Acceptance is not cementation; trace/measure separately |

### R1 account-scoped preparation reservations — 2026-10-21

The queue reuses ParallelBlockProcessor locks through a bounded nonwaiting reservation
API. The first queued candidate prepares; queued siblings share its guard and use
serialized admission. Sharing is necessary: merely dropping the first candidate's
guard after commit could let a later worker race an earlier queued sibling's serial
fallback. Reservations follow the authenticated candidate through commit/rejection
and cancelled next calls. Idle lock/weak entries are reclaimed; maps are bounded by
worker count. Serial eligible payments restore authoritative writer state so skipping
speculative capture cannot hide snapshot faults.

### R5 persistent rate activation and timestamp index (2026-10-21)

RateHistory now retains shared persistent segment vectors and a timestamp-keyed cumulative
accrual map. Rate activation changes the final segment, appends one segment and updates one
prefix entry, copying O(log R) tree paths instead of O(R) shared arrays. A same-time change
replaces the timestamp index entry with the last segment, preserving existing rate semantics.
Balance intervals retain O(log R) predecessor lookups, including checked 192-bit prefix
subtraction. Malformed raw histories still use the legacy checked scan; engine restoration
still rejects them. Cold chain validation uses adjacent iterators, avoiding indexed tree
lookups per segment. Cold map construction is O(R log R) conservatively; snapshots are O(1).

The segments accessor exposes the persistent indexed collection; two test-only Vec copies
were adapted. Serialized history remains exactly the old segment-vector encoding.59 BRN
and four storage-cache tests pass; a4096-segment regression verifies untouched chunk sharing,
candidate isolation, encoded bytes, valid accrual and rejected backward timestamps. Existing
properties cover duplicate times, overflow, malformed history and pauses. Receipts:
`brn-indexed-persistent-rates-20261021/corrected` and `brn-persistent-rate-cache-20261021`.
The initial map build failed on an unavailable OrdMap.last API; the corrected get_max build
passed. Historical vector-only pass and build failure remain recorded.

This removes in-memory shared detachment only. Aggregate serialization still costs O(R); equal-length independent comparison may scan,
while an append differs in length. cold reads and full exports remain whole-history operations. Normalized
storage must update the borrowed raw snapshot reader, full replacement, installed checkpoint
changes and undo together. Node integration and large-history memory/time diagnostics remain

### R5 normalized rate codec and proven appended suffix (2026-10-21)

Added local count/ordinal rows with fixed24-byte start/rate values. Segment ends are

field. Decode checks exact inventory/order/lengths and monotonic timestamps and allocates

### R2 origin trace: remove repeated whole-state scans — 2026-10-21

Found an additional CX14 query amplification path. `handle_trace_origin` built a
reverse adjacency map from every merge input, then scanned every token in every
wallet separately for each reachable merge, all under the live TRST mutex.
With global edges E, retained tokens T, reachable merges D and output rows R, the
avoidable work was O(E + D*T), in addition to reads and O(R log R) sorting.

The handler now shares the existing nonqueued read executor, captures persistent
graph/wallet roots under a short guard, follows the maintained origin-to-consumer
index and aggregates descendant holdings in one pass. Expected query work is
O(E_reachable + D log M + T + R log R), plus D merge-block reads (M is the global
merge-index size). Empty closures skip the holdings pass. Temporary retained work
is proportional to the reachable graph and output, rather than all graph edges;
one holder's temporary amount map is released before the next wallet.

The live-holder index cannot answer this historical RPC unchanged: it excludes
revoked chunks, whereas the response includes all token states. The fix preserves
those amounts, duplicate-path deduplication, null-holder historical total rows,
timestamp/hash/holder ordering, overflow rejection and original-burn validation.
It does not claim a global scan is constant-time, add a derived authoritative
index, or change signing or economic semantics. Snapshot isolation is intra-TRST;
block-store reads and the snapshot do not acquire a new cross-store atomic cut.

Focused RPC-only validation passed in trace-origin-host-20261021: build21.05s and
two exact regressions, final3-stage audit verified. Service is inactive/PID0/success.
The prior two worker-lifetime receipts also rechecked reusable. New regressions
cover a diamond and duplicate inputs, unrelated branches, revoked-only/mixed-state
holders, consumed merges, missing block error, checked overflow and retained roots
surviving later mutation. Prior worker behavior is unchanged. R2/full-state and
release gates remain open; this component change does not justify a payment rerun.


### R3/R5 remaining-scope reconciliation — 2026-10-21

Read-only source review; no build or scenario rerun. The previous trace change
has terminal passing evidence. This review distinguishes remaining implementation
from existing C16 work and corrects stale current payment metrics against the
saved cement-group/tests/034 terminal log (80 blocks, 25.411s, 3.148 blocks/s).
For clarity, the arithmetic median of80 samples is1.468743s; previous reports used
the upper-middle sample1.476615s. Their p95 is sorted index76 (6.189147s); nearest-rank
p95 is index75 (6.040226s). Neither convention changes the unmet latency requirement.
Historical failed loads and earlier measurements are unchanged.

**Recovery dispatch.** `store_lmdb/src/write_batch.rs::rewind_block_with_snapshots`
loads one block journal, verifies all current images and ledger positions, prepares
the retained inverse, applies raw rows and only then publishes the retained cut.
`trst/src/engine/restored_state.rs::retained_graph_rewind` first accepts fixed-topology
revision/contribution changes; otherwise it tries complete appended-node removal.
A mixed topology/revision journal or unsupported restoration returns None and uses
full reconstruction. Existing revision tests cover revocation, restoration, outcome
causes and surviving held bases. Therefore “revision-bearing removal always restores
global state” is stale. A multi-block fork alone does not prove a mixed *single*
journal. Before extending the inverse, identify a reachable producing operation or
an import/recovery contract requiring that mixture; do not weaken dependency checks
to make an artificial mixed-row fixture pass. Full-node recovery memory remains open.

**Supported retention behavior today.** Decisions10.2/10.4 already choose operator
pruning and peer history recovery. C16 in COMPLETION_PLAN already requires an atomic,
dependency-closed retained set. `ledger/src/pruning.rs::LedgerPruner` only selects
bounded candidates; repository references show no node consumer. It cannot establish
bounded disk growth or authorize deletion. Current operation retains restorable
TRST, graph ancestry/revisions, outcome causes, rate history and authority evidence.
Existing terminal cleanup is narrower: cemented undo pruning and finalized losing
fork payload cleanup enforce their own confirmation checks. Neither retires economic
rights or implements the requested archival mode.

| State | Retain while required by | Necessary archive/working-set boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expired holdings and origin times | Governance expiry extension and reputation | Preserve exact amount, origin/basis, owner and effective time in authenticated recoverable state; age alone cannot delete rights |
| Revoked chunks and graph revisions | Appeal restoration, contribution rounding, later composition bases | Preserve causes, revision dependencies and held/pending references; zero current spendability is insufficient |
| BRN rates, pauses and releases | Compute-on-read accrual and still-live stake/release accounting | Historical summaries must reproduce exact interval arithmetic and reversal behavior; no stale balance substitution |
| Provisional journals and fork rows | Allowed canonical rewind and outstanding confirmation decisions | Existing per-block confirmation guards remain; checkpoint advancement must prove exclusion or preservation |
| Governance/verification authority history | Historical quorum, selection, activation and recovery proof | Reuse C02/C03/C16 authenticated historical-reader/retirement boundary; a cold archive file alone is not an online reader |

This is the current supported behavior and required archive contract, not a new
pruning implementation or a population/memory guarantee. The131072-entry/64MiB
provisional migration budgets in node/brn_storage.rs and node/trst_storage.rs bound
migration journal collection, not supported lifetime ledger size. The TRST legacy
snapshot64MiB decode ceiling is a separate format constraint. Neither may be raised
or reinterpreted as production capacity. Full-state activation pause, steady-state
working set and recoverable archive implementation remain R5/C16 obligations.

Next implementation boundary: reuse the existing C02/C03/C16 historical reader and
checkpoint-retirement work; prove missing state can be recovered and validated before
any physical pruning. Existing counter benchmarks do not answer this question and
must not be repeated to claim closure. No source whitepaper or owner choice changed.


### R3 owned checkpoint payload copies on panel cache hits — 2026-10-21

The historical reader is implemented; do not repeat the earlier vector-to-source
migration plan. SelectionHistory reconstructs an owned CertifiedCheckpoint, while
Panels cached it as Cow::Owned and cloned that payload on every cache hit and cache
insertion. CertifiedCheckpoint owns two head vectors through Record/ReplayedCheckpoint,
certificate proof data and optional replay history hashes. Existing roster sharing
alone does not avoid these copies. Repeated access to one panel therefore still paid
O(certificate payload) per hit despite only one authenticated source lookup.

Panels now retains borrowed certificates as references and owned certificates as Arc.
A hit clones only the handle; the panel and cache share the same immutable payload.
The one-entry limit, source-borrow lifetime, disk-row checks, checkpoint/context/position
validation and final durable-history guards are unchanged. Source lookup on cache miss
still authenticates the full historical source; no trusted on-disk shortcut was added.

The existing scoped-reuse regression now checks pointer identity across32 cache hits
for both source ownership modes and both panel storage modes, while preserving damaged
row, wrong identity and new replay checks. Capped node build and three focused replay
cases passed in panel-sharing-host-20261021 (94s build;0.146s,0.143s,1.077s tests).
Final4-stage receipt audit passes and evidence archive hash is verified in the ledger.
No public latency, memory or release
qualification is inferred from this structural improvement.


### R4 replay default selection and repeated completion hashing — 2026-10-21

In Selections::install_for, prior-panel replay iterated V voters; each performed a
linear search across C completions and absent lists, cloned a matching Completion,
and encoded/hashed that complete absent list again. A panel with A absent voters
could therefore repeat O(A) commitment work for each of those voters, in addition
to O(V*C) searches through unrelated completions.

The replay-only helper now builds a borrowed needed-voter set, visits completions
in the original order, skips other targets/lifecycles, and removes each matched
voter once. A relevant completion is encoded/hashed only when it contributes its
first needed voter; its exact original commitment is reused for subsequent matches.
Expected work is O(V+C+A_relevant), including one encoding per contributing record;
extra selection memory is O(V). Overlapping records retain the original first-match
behavior. Empty/no-match results and exact hashes/deadlines are preserved. The
existing completion validator, prior-panel history commitment and signed settlement
checks remain. Live ledger read/decoding cost is separate and unchanged.

Extended the existing lifecycle regression to compare128 voters and overlapping
completions against the original lookup, with two contributing-record hashes counted.
One node-test build plus this and the existing normal/challenge revote integration
checks passed in replay-defaults-host-20261021: build70s; normal0.673s, challenge2.197s,
lifecycle parity0.020s. The latter verifies two hashes for128 prior voters; final4-stage
receipt audit passes and the downloaded evidence archive hash is verified. Prior integration receipts audited
before source sync; unchanged payment and load tests are not repeated.


### R4 metadata default reader amplification — 2026-10-21

Both live_history_commitment and ConfirmedReplay::selection_history_commitment
read each prior voter's binding then decoded/cloned/hashed its completion body.
For V voters sharing an A-member absent list this repeated O(V*A) decoding,
validation, membership and commitment work. The prior replay-list fix did not
cover these two metadata readers.

Both callers now group the V bindings by context with a BTreeMap, then decode each
of C distinct referenced completion bodies once and hash it once if the lifecycle
matches. The decoder validates sorted unique absent addresses; membership uses binary
search. Expected bound is O(V log C + sum A + V log A), including encoding/hashing
of each relevant body, with O(V + max A) temporary state. Bindings are still read
individually and every body/target/context/voter is validated before lifecycle skipping.
There is no cross-call trust cache. Replay gains the same context-binding rejection
already required by the live reader; valid metadata produces identical commitments.

The existing128-voter test now checks two reads/two hashes in each lifecycle mode,
old-result parity, absent/wrong/malformed bindings, target/context/member/order guards,
read errors and valid different-lifecycle exclusion. Normal/challenge revote settlement
and live activation/late-vote cases are selected. Capped host build and four exact
cases passed in default-reader-host-20261021: build71s; activation0.386s, normal
revote0.673s, challenge revote2.231s, lifecycle/read/hash regression0.022s. Final5-stage
receipt audit passes; downloaded archive hash verified in the ledger. This does not establish full-node or
release performance, and does not change signing, deadlines or economic rules.

### CX11 warm typed-wallet persistence — 2026-10-21

Source trace found a second full-history pass after wallet serialization:
`AuxiliaryCache::update_brn` decoded the freshly encoded row, rebuilding pending
release roots and indexes. `put_brn_wallet_state` now serializes the supplied typed
state, detaches the optional warm cache, delegates all raw bytes, undo recording,
mutation flags and failure poisoning to the original writer, and republishes a
cloned typed state with checked old/new raw-byte accounting. Both node full/delta
BRN persistence paths use it. The cache is discarded on write failure or invalid
accounting; raw adapters and rewind keep their original decode/invalidation path.
There is no caller-supplied byte/state pair that could disagree.

This removes an O(releases + proof entries) warm decode/index-rebuild pass, while
canonical encoding, before/after comparison and journal storage remain linear in
the touched wallet bytes. Wallet cloning also still copies paused intervals. It
is not a constant-time wallet-write claim or a new measured payment speedup.
`BrnSnapshot::wallet_entries`, signed-history replay mutation recording, checkpoint
changes and raw undo currently all consume complete wallet rows. Removing that
remaining encoding/write amplification requires coordinated storage/reader/undo
migration, retaining exact replay and historical rights; a cache change alone
cannot close it. Genesis initialization writes an empty wallet once; installed
checkpoint changes intentionally remain raw encoded-row writes.

Validation is recorded in the ledger: combined store/node build passed,15 cases
passed, and the new fixture failed only at construction of an invalid address.
Its correction creates corruption through the raw writer, then requires that a
valid typed write cannot hide it. Storage-only rebuild passed in23.42s and the corrected exact case passed in0.122s;
seven node passes and eight prior cache passes remain applicable. Final17-stage
audit passes; archives and hashes are recorded in the current ledger. The original

### CX11 coordinated wallet-row migration groundwork — 2026-10-21

The locality trace identified a required coupling: live BRN writes produce undo
via the transaction writer, while checkpoint recovery independently emits complete
wallet before/after images in `installed/changes/recorded.rs`. `Rows::capture`,
`Rows::stage`, raw adapters, bounded writer reads and checkpoint clearing also
assume complete wallet rows. A live-only normalized writer would make reconstructed
undo disagree with physical state. Existing authenticated stable-holdings/rate
migration in installed/metadata.rs supplies the integration pattern: stage matching
state and provisional journals together before committing a format change.

Added `brn::wallet_storage` as a shared, not-yet-active codec. Relative records carry
a scalar/count header, one row per paused interval, and one row per release proof.
The release delta visitor skips shared tree nodes; only changed proofs are encoded.
A scalar edit emits one row regardless of release backlog. Pause comparison remains
O(P); full construction/decoding remains proportional to the inventory. No current
storage format, signing, balance calculation or malformed-proof fallback changed.

The codec decoder requires a complete ordered inventory, exact key/value encodings,
counts and version; it does not preallocate from header counts. Existing checked
PendingReleases reconstruction rebuilds derived indexes without opening its private
mutation methods. Three focused tests cover1024-release row deltas and inverse
application, complete-row/legacy-byte parity, create/delete, sink failure, twelve
corruption shapes/read failure, overflow accounting and conservative malformed-proof
selection. After correcting an initial visibility compile error, BRN-only build2.34s
and all three tests passed; final four-stage audit passes. Retained failure and
passing receipts/archives are identified in the completion ledger.

This is migration groundwork, not a persistence-performance result. Next connect
readers, cache accounting, raw writes/delete, authenticated projection/undo and
migration selection coherently, then extend the existing storage and recorded-vs-full
projection tests. The full-row write amplification finding stays open until those
active paths and recovery compatibility pass; no throughput/release gate closes here.


### CX11 normalized wallet storage branch — 2026-10-21

Storage can now read/write the wallet-record codec under an explicit format marker;
no production path selects that marker yet. Headers reside in BrnWallets, child rows
in length-framed address namespaces in BrnMeta. Namespaces permit arbitrary existing
UTF-8 local address bytes without prefix collisions. Unknown format markers, children
without a marker, orphan children, misplaced headers and malformed inventories fail.
Warm typed writes emit persistent deltas, match each old physical row, use the normal
undo/poisoning path and republish shared cache state with exact physical-byte changes.
Raw header/child writes invalidate the cache. Bounded cold reads check wallet count,
charge the orphan scan and charge child bytes before decoding. Delete and checkpoint
clearing remove child rows; independent adapters retain generation invalidation.

BrnSnapshot now returns Cow bytes: legacy views borrow rows, normalized canonical-byte
views reconstruct one wallet. This preserves the adapter contract and pinned views but
currently adds a cold encode/decode round trip in BrnEngine::load_from_store. That is
an explicit remaining cost, not a claimed cold-path improvement. Physical namespace
bytes count toward restoration limits; migration row/work-budget coverage still needs
review as complete wallets expand into separate proof/interval records.

Two new storage tests and eleven existing BRN snapshot/cache checks pass. The1024-proof
case demonstrates one scalar undo row, two rows for scalar-plus-release insertion,
less than256 encoded after-image bytes in each case, shared warm proof identities,
exact warm/cold limits, raw adapter parity, pinned reads, rewind, abort, reopen, deletion
and projection clear. The corruption case checks cached invalidation and rejected raw
format/orphan/header changes. Initial compile-test visibility and same-thread nested
read fixture failures were diagnosed and retained. Only the failed/unexecuted cases
ran after correcting reader lifetime; seven passes were reused. Final14-stage audit
passes; current ledger identifies all receipts and hashes.

Next: connect authenticated recovery capture/recorded changes/staging and matching
provisional journal migration before selecting the format. No production activation,
node integration, throughput, full-memory or release qualification is claimed here.

### Admission grouping constraints (2026-10-22; source review, not implemented)

The current transaction owns one UndoRecorder. begin_block_undo rejects both dirty
transactions and an existing recorder. ledger_updater::stage_block invokes that
boundary for every block; commit consumes and encodes it. commit_elected_block
seals it only as part of a terminal commit/handoff. Resetting dirty or overwriting
the recorder to loop over blocks would bypass existing replay/rewind guards.
Per-block journal keys and before-values must remain separate in any grouped cut;
a later block must record the preceding staged state, not the pre-group snapshot.

Admission also publishes live economics, frontier and processor state before
validating the next block. A grouped implementation must validate against staged
state, preserve shared-source conflicts, and defer every publication, dependency
release, acceptance response and local vote until commit. Merely moving the commit
call outside the existing loop is invalid. RwTxn is not Send, so awaiting next()
with a live transaction is incompatible with the current owned worker future.

BlockValidationQueue owns bounded FIFO authentication handles and keeps a pending
head across cancellation. It exposes one result at a time; no cancellation-safe
ready-group API exists. The configured worker count can be one, leaving no queued
prepared result while that result is admitted. Creating an arbitrary group by
waiting for more input would add latency and interfere with the biased shutdown,
snapshot and fork-install branches. Group only already-ready work, with explicit
size/byte bounds and singleton fallback after an atomic abort; do not add a fill timer.

Next implementation boundary is the storage journal grouping contract together
with its admission caller, not an isolated relaxation of begin_block_undo. Required
regressions already have bases in write_batch undo tests, prepared-payment
rebase/reopen/rewind tests, block_validation cancellation tests and node startup
admission/fault tests. Keep the optimized candidate immutable until that coherent
change is ready; no build is needed for this review or summary reconciliation.

### R5 mutation coverage review — 2026-10-24

This is a source audit of the current candidate, not a runtime pass or permission
to reuse across ordinary commits. The latest node build and10affected checks were
re-audited on their evidence host: all11receipts still report reusable/pass;
owned unit is inactive/MainPID0. No build, test, payment workload or daemon rerun.
Reviewed file hashes are retained in
`target/validation-evidence/undo-copy-node-20261024/retirement-write-review.json`.

The concrete capture boundary must include these paths. This table describes
observed behavior; the proposed capture/invalidation handling is not implemented.

| Current writer path | What bypasses `mutate_raw` | Required handling before wider reuse |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write_batch.rs::mutate_raw` | Primary value reaches one put/delete; verified-account, pending-sender/amount and graph-position helpers also update derived indexes | Capture the semantic table/key mutation, with bounded image bytes; derived indexes do not independently authorize dropping roots |
| `write_batch.rs::commit_elected_block` | Writes finished undo directly, then records confirmation handoff | Preserve block/journal carrier and all staged root additions; sealing must be covered before publishing the commit interval |
| `write_batch/block_group.rs::seal_block_undo` | Direct journal put occurs for every block, including intermediate grouped blocks | Do not observe only the final journal or final per-key image; preserve intermediate block requirements |
| `write_batch/verification_records.rs::replace_verification_target_undo` | Direct normalized-row put/delete after virtual target expansion | Capture the actual changed normalized rows or invalidate; watching only the virtual key misses physical roots |
| `verification_records.rs::replace_verification_undo_snapshot` | Direct writes after aggregate expansion | Capture expanded changes or invalidate the entire dependency proof |
| `verification_records.rs::{migrate_verification_records,normalize_verification_records}` | Direct legacy-image deletion and normalized row installation | Treat layout changes as invalidation until all reference extraction and format dependencies are qualified |
| `governance_records.rs::replace_governance_undo_snapshot` | Direct record removal/replacement owned by aggregate undo | Capture expanded changes or invalidate; aggregate undo presence is not coverage |
| `governance_records.rs::{replace_checkpoint_governance_records,migrate_governance_records}` | Direct old aggregate deletion plus namespace replacement | Invalidate certified-cut/layout assumptions; never call migration a harmless metadata write |
| `checkpoint_projection.rs::clear_checkpoint_rows` | No-prefix branch clears a primary table and derived indexes directly; prefix branch deletes through `delete_raw` | Whole-table clear needs an explicit invalidation event, not an empty changed-key list |
| `meta.rs::commit_vote_reservation` and other self-committing stores | Separate native transactions, outside the write-batch recorder | Keep exact native-generation gap rejection. Only the existing typed all-soft sequence interval is proven safe; final votes/checkpoint promises are not covered |

Root coverage also extends beyond the existing economic replay-image decoder:

| Required roots | Existing source/decoder | Why a generic undo decoder is insufficient |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TRST holdings, wallet/graph rows, pending transfers | `store_lmdb/src/retention.rs`; `bodies/replayed.rs::image` | Pending source is a block address, while token/transaction/graph identities must not be cast to block hashes |
| BRN, verification receipts/state, governance, scoped delegation | `bodies.rs::collect` and typed retention visitors | Reuse typed decoders with network/genesis and format checks; unsupported prefixes invalidate |
| Account heads and pending confirmations | `retention/account_work.rs` | Confirmation work is deliberately irreversible and absent from ordinary block undo |
| Payment signing promises | `metadata/retention/signers.rs`, payment promise decoder | Final/fence records can introduce required bodies; soft counter coverage does not extend to them |
| Checkpoint round manifests, signer selections, selection receipts | `metadata/retention/rounds.rs` and `bodies.rs::collect` | Manifest heads are roots; epoch IDs and commitments alone are not body references |
| Undo carrier and authenticated before/after dependencies | `bodies.rs::body_requirements`, `visit_rollback_body_roots`, `bodies/replayed.rs::replayed_change` | Local stored undo bytes are not authenticated replay. Existing extractor deliberately accepts opaque replay-derived records |
| Applied suffix and its dependencies | `bodies.rs::collect` archive visitor | Intermediate applied blocks remain required even when no current frontier names them |

Two approaches are ruled out by this review: inferring completeness from the
common mutation hook alone, and repurposing coalesced persisted undo as a change
feed. `UndoRecorder::record` removes net-zero A→B→A updates. Grouped transactions
also seal more than one block before commit. A complete feed must account for
those boundaries and publish coverage only after successful native commit.

The next implementation boundary is one optional, bounded in-process feed of
covered mutations plus explicit invalidation. It must be inactive when no
retirement owner exists, bound accumulated bytes/entries before copying, reject
overflow/gaps/reopen/foreign environments, and never turn missing coverage into
an empty delta. A consumer may only remove candidates from an already-authenticated
eligibility catalogue while adding newly required roots and checking their closure;
changed epoch/layout or unknown dependencies require fresh preparation. The writer
must recheck the exact reconciled cut before deletion. Restart authentication and
initial inventory limits remain separate unresolved requirements. This describes
the necessary contract, not an implemented feature or a completed R5 gate.


### R5 initial inventory dependency contract — 2026-10-24

Source review distinguishes four independent jobs. Persisting ancestry inputs
solves repeated acquisition; it does not by itself make physical inventory,
required-body closure or deletion eligibility restart-authenticated.

| Consumer / source | Required invariant | Consequence for resumable inventory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `store_lmdb/src/block/inventory.rs::IndexedBlockCursor` | Every physical body has matching forward/reverse position; all three counts match in one pinned view | A bookmark is traversal state only. Finishing one window cannot claim global completeness; a new read view needs an explicit mutation reconciliation proof. |
| `snapshot/installed/retained.rs::plan` | Observation digest/account/height match physical bytes; committed heads and retained account rows authenticate against the certified base | Persisted observations are raw input. Never reconstruct a `HistoricalBlock` or trusted cursor solely from saved row metadata. |
| `RetainedInventory::observed_body` and `metadata::resolve_body` | Exact observed bytes and authenticated position determine body origin | A missing window is unknown, not an absent or deletable body. Random lookup must cover every completed partition and reject incomplete/corrupt coverage. |
| `RetainedInventory::capture_successor` | Each successor row is inherited from authenticated prior state or supplied authenticated installation | Partitioning must preserve the ordered merge and installation proof, not merely current physical membership. |
| `RetainedInventory::verify_unchanged` | Complete physical/account inventory agrees under the publication writer, unless a valid unchanged cut proves reuse | Persisted native transaction numbers alone cannot skip this check. `CleanStorageCut` includes live environment identity and deliberately carries no authentication authority. |
| `BodyRequirements::collect` / `ClosureWalk` | All economic, signer, round, replay and rollback roots have complete dependency closure | Closure limits are independent of inventory limits. A larger inventory backend alone cannot qualify retirement at larger retained sizes. |
| `ClosedBodyRequirements::own_retirement` | Every original candidate is classified under one complete checked closure; later observations only revoke eligibility | A partially classified catalogue cannot delete. Epoch/layout change or missing change coverage must invalidate the catalogue. |

The current whole-attempt inventory ceiling charges raw body/index bytes, while
its scratch builder separately charges encoded observation bytes. Physical file
allocation and the shared scratch reservation are different measurements again.
A future partition implementation must report each separately; treating a page
budget as a reset of total accounting would hide the capacity failure.

The authenticated chain presently supplies predecessor links, not skip proofs.
Checking an untrusted old ancestor from a certified head therefore requires
traversing the intervening chain. The unavoidable total traversal is distinct
from avoidable repeat network acquisition and from unbounded work between
shutdown checks. Durable inputs address acquisition; local-history-pages addresses
the latter scheduling gap. Neither claims constant-time restart authentication.

Decisions6.9 and6.15 explicitly allow expiry extension and re-verification to
restore transferability;10.2 makes pruning operator-configurable and10.4 retains
peer history recovery. The whitepaper's pruning statement cannot be implemented
by discarding those restoration rights. This review changes no economic rule,
limit or production gate. Remaining implementation must compose complete bounded
partitions, conservative mutation coverage, authenticated reopening and closure,
then qualify disk overhead and service rate using retained immutable fixtures.

Source review found two constraints that change the implementation path:
- `Pending::commit` holds the observer State mutex through native commit; capture
  coverage/visitation also needs it. A native allocation callback cannot wait for
  capture cleanup while holding that mutex.
- Admission holds economic/lifecycle guards before opening its writer, converts
  storage errors into strings, and only retries grouped staging before commit is
  attempted. Capture cancellation/retry must preserve ownership and release these
  guards before waiting. Generic commit/I/O errors must not become retryable.
Locked LMDB commit source routes allocation/freelist errors to transaction abort
before writing the new meta page. This supports distinguishing native MapFull;
it does not prove safe retry after every possible commit error.
Sub-store direct writers also open native transactions outside LmdbWriteTransaction;
a limit implemented only in payment mutation methods cannot cover the environment.
